text:
Elaine (CS): Quick async standup — pre-renewal check for Zephyr.ai. Adoption metrics dipped ~15% overnight and we observed a burst of webhook 500s around 02:10 UTC. TL;DR: I gathered logs + a customer repro, escalated to eng. Blockers: need a patch and a short mitigation note before the Wed renewal call. Today: coordinate deploy, draft customer message.

Marco (Eng): Looking through the logs — looks like connection-pool exhaustion on our dedicated delivery pool when payloads spike. Same pattern we saw in last month's load run. I opened PR #1423 that adds jittered backoff + a small connection cap and a circuit-breaker for the webhook sender. @Elaine, is Zephyr on our SDK retry default or did they customize retries?

Elaine (CS): They're on the default SDK settings (5 retries exponential). They also use a fairly aggressive concurrency from their worker fleet.

Ben (SRE): Temp mitigation applied: ulimit raised on the zephyr pool nodes and nginx keepalive bumped to 90s. Watching metrics. If Marco's PR lands we can canary.

Marco (Eng): Pushed a short deploy guide in the PR description. Snippet: `git checkout fix/pool-backoff && ./deploy.sh --canary zephyr-pool`

Tom (Eng Reviewer): I'll review PR #1423 today, target 10:30 PT. If tests are green, Ben — can you run the smoke suite and promote to prod canary?

Ben (SRE): Smoke tests running now. Quick sanity so far. Will post results.

eng-bot: Note: incident-1234 created for zephyr-webhook-500s. Severity: low -> escalating to oncall if errors persist.

Priya (CS Lead): For the renewal call: propose offering a 30-day extension as a goodwill gesture if we need additional time. Elaine can you draft the language? Keep it short and avoid technical details unless asked. :memo:

Elaine (CS): Will draft. Also planning to propose a temporary client-side rate limit recommendation and point them to the SDK version with the fix once deployed.

Ben (SRE): Smoke suite finished — staging passed at 1k req/min synthetic for 15m with no 500s. Ready to canary on prod pool after approval. Logs: https://ci.internal/zephyr/472

Marco (Eng): Thanks. If Tom approves, I'll queue the canary. After canary we should monitor: 95p latency, 500s, and connection_wait_count.

Tom (Eng Reviewer): PR approved — left one tiny nit. Marco: once you address, I'll merge.

Marco (Eng): Fixed nit and pushed. Merge after CI.

deploybot: canary deploy started for zephyr-prod-pool build=472. Link: https://deploys.internal/zephyr/472 — monitoring hooks attached.

Ben (SRE): Canary running — initial 10% traffic slice showing 0 errors across 30m. I'll ramp to 30% in 20m if stable.

Priya (CS Lead): Great. Elaine, hold the renewal wording until we see 30% green. If Ben sees anomalies, we'll offer the extension and propose a short joint tech call. Finance wants a churn-risk blurb ready in case.

Elaine (CS): Understood. Draft ready but will wait to send. I'll ping Zephyr's renewal contact after 30% ramp with a status note and ETA. :thumbsup:

Ben (SRE): 30% ramped, still clean. Monitoring for next 45m then final decision to full roll.

Marco (Eng): If all good, plan is: merge -> full rollout -> post-rollout add a metric to alert on connection_wait_count > 20/min.

Elaine (CS): Thanks team. I'll update the renewal thread with this timeline and the contingency text. If anything changes, I'll ping here.

Priya (CS Lead): Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Tom (Eng Reviewer): LGTM.

Elaine (CS): Closing loop — will post customer-facing note once full rollout finishes.
